candidates.original_title: The Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI): A multidimensional self-report instrument for the assessment of female sexual function
candidates.description: The original FSFI study validated the six-factor structure and psychometric properties of the Female Sexual Function Index in a clinical sample; this replication evaluates whether those psychometric properties (factor structure, internal consistency, construct validity) hold in an unselected twin sample.
candidates.notes: The paper uses reference number [12] rather than explicitly naming the original authors and year in the text body; the original study is Rosen et al. (2000) as cited in reference [12]. The replication evaluates the FSFI's six-factor structure, internal consistency, and CFA fit in a twin sample (N=744 for EFA, N=930 for the FSFI subsample). The authors explicitly state 'we were successful in replicating the six-factor structure of the original FSFI.' The FSFI-LL development and validation is a separate new instrument contribution, not a replication entry.

candidates.original_title: The Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI): A multidimensional self-report instrument for the assessment of female sexual function
candidates.description: The original FSFI has a six-factor structure corresponding to desire, arousal, lubrication, orgasm, satisfaction, and pain, with adequate psychometric properties.
candidates.citation_sentence: Based on the EFA findings and clinical considerations presented in previous reports, a six-factor model was hypothesized for the CFA of the original FSFI [12,20,21].
candidates.notes: The paper also develops and validates the modified FSFI-LL, but that is an extension rather than a replication of a separately published study. The paper uses numbered citations rather than author-year citations; citation [12] identifies Rosen et al. (2000).
